item.title: Needs edits
item.content:encoded:
Hi all,

I noticed and editted a spelling mistake (rood instead of rod) and grammer error ("for exhaust to exit" not "to exhaust to exit"). Also the "hot gas rush causes …" didn't really seem to make sense grammatically so I changed to to "and inhalation of hot gases causing …"

Hope that is alright.

Also the part about the emissions is kinda interesting but drums and barrels are not really mentioned anywhere else in the text making it a bit jarring and confusing about what is actually being referred to.

So this article is fairly short, and due to its brevity it's a bit challenging to find something to work into the article that wouldn't disrupt the rhythm it maintains throughout it. However, this article does mention a site that has a site dossier which links to all of the other objects that are kept at that particular site which would allow readers to discover the other objects that are contained there as well as learn more about the site itself.

Editing this:

SCP-240 is to be kept in the Secure Artifact Storage Facility in Site-77.

To read:

SCP-240 is to be kept in the Secure Artifact Storage Facility in Site-77.

Additionally, since the UIU is mentioned in the article, I'd like to propose a link to the UIU hub itself.

Editing this:

It was found inside the home and taken as evidence by the UIU.

To read:

It was found inside the home and taken as evidence by the UIU.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Not sure if this is running on universe-power per se, just that air is being passed through another universe whose law of physics does not conserve momentum like ours does. At most, maybe the wording on that reveal could be better-paced. It certainly didn't really feel out of left field for me, and overall felt quite cute. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I agree about the writing and the extra dimensions yet thought it still deserved my upvote.

One more thing that bugged me though:

fiber optic camera technology

That doesn't really mean anything. Fiber optics relates to wiring and information transfer, with very little to do with cameras. Unless there is a meaning I am not recognizing, this could be simplified to "using ranged cameras", or removal of the whole solar system bit.

By the way, has anyone else thought of what could happen if the "exhaust pipes" were directed back into the mouth piece? It would be a literally exponential growth of energy and the foundation for a perpetual motion device! Are there any other SCPs that have or could have been used this way?

(Also yes, I know that I'm a little late to the party on this discussion, wanted to say something anyways)

"…the camera recorded a location in space which appeared very similar to the solar system. However, the Earth and Moon were missing and Venus had several possibly artificial satellites around it."

You can see all that from the inside of a tube, huh? This is certainly better than the atrocious original, but that's not saying much.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This really moves up the origin of the UIU to the early 1920s. My headcannon was always 60-70s, very Joe Friday/Get Smart-ish. Now that I think about it, I had no reason for that assumption. Now I'm just imagining Elliot Ness at the start of Untouchables (the film version) with the umbrella.

Anyways, not a fan of the line " These emissions contain minerals such as nickel, copper, gold, platinum, potassic feldspar, and Pyroxferroite." For one, four of the six things listed are elements, not minerals. Second, this seems like a very imprecise way of listing the emissions.

I also agree with the fact that their is not enough lead up for the 'boom, another universe in the mouthpiece' thing to not seem like it is out of nowhere. Feel like there is potential, but it is not yet realized. Neutral vote for now.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This feels like the same article with GoIs shoehorned in to generate interest. I also echo the comments above about the addendum; that is waaaaaaay too short to do anything but make the reader go "huh?".

About the "bootlegging" thing. Firstly, that's an informal term that probably wouldn't show up in a scientific document. Secondly, you don't get charged formally with "bootlegging". Thirdly, bootlegging refers to the illegal smuggling and transport of alcohol, not its illicit manufacture, which is what I think you're meaning to refer to there.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I liked it enough to upvote, but that addendum really is kind of jarring for me. There must be a more subtle way to indicate extra-universal presence than "Hey, there's a solar system making this thing go. Come take a picture." Those hints in the dust barrels and the mouthpiece are almost enough. Maybe just a few more of them.

That said, I can't help but be curious about how the hell these people made a flying machine that runs on universe-power. The tale possibilities of this version are a large part of what's keeping this from a neutral vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I understand that. It still doesn't change my opinion of it seemingly being put in without rhyme or reason.

There are better ways to show that something is from a different world/reality than by shoving a solar system into the object; Alexyvia University skips tend to do it well.

Anyway, that's all my opinion. Not like my downvote alone is an indicator of how the community at large feels, or that this article won't do well.
